builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
summary: The method replaces repeated reasoning callbacks after tool feedback with guarded reuse of previously resolved decisions stored as Executable Decision Graphs, substituting certified callbacks through the native interface while actor weights remain fixed. It costs the engineering complexity of a controller at the model-tool boundary, RSI-based refinement of harness configurations with validation, and the infrastructure for storing graphs with literal arguments, causal dependencies, and guards. It can fail when new semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, or selector abstention force fallback to the original actor, and gains are benchmark-dependent on repeated-decision structure that production workloads may not exhibit.
rationale: Token savings up to 87.93% with preserved or improved success directly benefit a constrained-budget team, but the method requires building non-trivial controller and graph infrastructure whose benefits depend on how repetitive the reader's actual agent workloads are, so a small-scale pilot is warranted before adoption.
technique: Guarded decision reuse in agent harnesses

claims.statement: The method replaces repeated reasoning callbacks after tool feedback with guarded reuse of previously resolved decisions stored as Executable Decision Graphs, substituting certified callbacks through the native interface while actor weights remain fixed. It costs the engineering complexity of a controller at the model-tool boundary, RSI-based refinement of harness configurations with validation, and the infrastructure for storing graphs with literal arguments, causal dependencies, and guards. It can fail when new semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, or selector abstention force fallback to the original actor, and gains are benchmark-dependent on repeated-decision structure that production workloads may not exhibit.

On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82% while reducing tokens per task from 66.72k to 47.02k (29.54% saving); for DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43% to 85.71% while tokens fall from 96.28k to 11.62k (87.93% saving, roughly 8.3x cost reduction); MBPP ablation shows 26.91% lower cost than single-use graphs.
